finding.title: The refund window is 90 days in one requirement and 30 days in another
finding.wrong_outcome: an implementer who follows the stated text as written builds a refund check that accepts a refund 60 days after capture because `A refund may be issued for any captured charge within 90 days of the capture date.` (S:13), and also rejects the same request because `A refund request older than 30 days after capture is rejected with the error code REFUND_EXPIRED.` (S:15). No implementation can satisfy both for a request 60 days after capture, and the acceptance test for refunds cannot be written.

e1.text: A refund may be issued for any captured charge within 90 days of the capture date.
e1.context:
R4. After the third failed attempt the charge moves to state failed and the customer is notified by email.

## 3. Refunds
R5. A refund may be issued for any captured charge within 90 days of the capture date.
R6. The refund amount may not exceed the captured amount minus refunds already issued for that charge.
R7. A refund request older than 30 days after capture is rejected with the error code REFUND_EXPIRED.
R8. Every refund creates one ledger entry of type refund in the same transaction as the state change.
